description: UI Bridge State Machine page — connect to SDK-integrated apps, discover UI states via automated exploration or manual recording with fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis, then manage state machine configs across six tabs: Discovery (SDK app connection, explore/record data collection, fingerprint-based state discovery with save), Graph Editor (interactive dagre node-edge layout with element thumbnails and drag-and-drop), State View (list + detail panel via shared StateViewPanel), Transitions (list with action playback via shared TransitionsPanel), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states via shared PathfindingPanel), and Export (save to JSON file or load into runtime).

groups.name: Discovery Algorithm Correctness
groups.description: The fingerprint-based state discovery algorithm groups UI elements by co-occurrence (95% threshold), position zone, and landmark context. It identifies global elements (>80% appearance in header/footer), modal states, and repeating patterns. Confidence scores are computed from observation count (log scale), element count, and size weighting. These assertions define what correct discovery output looks like — verifiable from the Discovery Complete card and the State View/Graph Editor tabs after saving.

assertions.description: Every discovered state must contain at least one element fingerprint. A state with zero elements indicates a grouping error in the discovery algorithm (min_state_elements: 1).
assertions.expected: Every state shown in the discovery preview and subsequently in the State View tab should have at least one element. The discovery algorithm enforces min_state_elements: 1.
assertions.precondition: Discovery has completed with results displayed

assertions.description: All discovered state confidence percentages should be between 1% and 100%. Values outside this range indicate a scoring bug.
assertions.expected: Every confidence value shown in the state preview list should be between 1% and 100% inclusive. Confidence is calculated from observation count (log scale), element count, and size weighting. States with more observations and significant elements should have higher confidence.
assertions.precondition: Discovery has completed with results displayed

assertions.description: No two discovered states should have identical element/fingerprint groupings. If two states show identical elements, the co-occurrence merging (95% threshold) failed to merge them.
assertions.expected: Each discovered state should have a unique set of elements. No two state cards in the State View tab should display identical element lists. The algorithm groups by position zone + landmark context, so states from different zones should be distinct.
assertions.precondition: Discovery completed and config saved with at least two states

assertions.description: A 'Save to File' button with Download icon exports the config as JSON via Tauri's save dialog
assertions.precondition: A config is selected, Export tab active

assertions.description: A 'Load into Runtime' button with Upload icon POSTs the config to /state-machine/load for live use
assertions.precondition: A config is selected, Export tab active

assertions.description: The export tab displays config name, state count, and transition count
assertions.expected: The export info should show: 'Config: [config name]' (bold), '{N} states', '{N} transitions'.
assertions.precondition: A config is selected, Export tab active

assertions.description: Clicking Save to File opens Tauri's save dialog and exports the config as JSON
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Save to File' should open Tauri's file save dialog with default filename '{configName}_state_machine.json'. The button shows Loader2 spinner during export and is disabled during the operation. On success, a toast notification confirms the save.
assertions.precondition: A config is selected, Export tab active

assertions.description: Clicking Load into Runtime POSTs the config JSON to the runtime API endpoint
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Load into Runtime' should POST the config JSON to /state-machine/load. The button shows Loader2 spinner during loading and is disabled during any operation. On success, a toast notification confirms the load.
assertions.precondition: A config is selected, Export tab active

groups.name: Toast Notifications
groups.description: The page uses a ToastContainer to display success and error notifications for operations like export, save, load into runtime, and discovery errors.

assertions.description: A ToastContainer is rendered at the bottom of the page for displaying notification messages
assertions.expected: A ToastContainer component should be rendered at the bottom of the page, ready to display success and error toast messages.

assertions.description: A success toast appears after successful export or load operations
assertions.expected: After a successful 'Save to File' or 'Load into Runtime' operation, a green success toast should appear briefly at the bottom of the page confirming the action.
assertions.precondition: An export or load operation completed successfully

assertions.description: An error toast appears when operations fail, showing the error reason
assertions.expected: When an operation fails (export, load, discovery, save), a red error toast should appear at the bottom of the page showing the error message/reason.
assertions.precondition: An operation has failed
